label: sc07 data structure from header
text: DATA FACTS (from file header only, no analysis): 158542059.node is an AnnData h5ad, 100,000 cells x 40,352 genes; X is a sparse CSR float32 matrix holding RAW integer-valued counts (no layers, no obsm, so no precomputed normalisation or PCA). obs has cell_type (18 levels), cytokine (91 levels), donor (12 levels), treatment (2 levels: PBS, cytokine), sample (1092 levels = 12 x 91, named Donor_Cytokine), plus split-pool barcode wells (bc1_well, bc2_well, bc3_well), tscp_count, gene_count, pct_counts_MT. Average is about 92 cells per sample and about 5 cells per sample-by-cell-type group.

label: PITFALL define PC1 variance explained as per-factor R2
text: PITFALL: 'Variance explained in PC1 by a factor' is confused with other quantities (PC1's share of total variance, gene loadings, or the scIB/kBET PCR score that sums over many PCs). The standard definition (scater getExplanatoryPCs, kBET pcRegression, scib pc_regression) is the R-squared of a one-factor-at-a-time linear regression of the PC1 scores on the one-hot-encoded factor, i.e. SS_between/SS_total (eta-squared) of PC1 across the factor's levels; it is marginal and unadjusted. CHECK: for each of the four factors compute 1 - RSS/TSS of PC1 score ~ C(factor) separately, on PC1 only. IF FOUND that you computed something else: recompute as marginal per-factor R-squared on PC1 and rank those. SOURCE: https://rdrr.io/bioc/scater/src/R/getVarianceExplained.R ; https://rdrr.io/bioc/scater/man/getExplanatoryPCs.html ; https://scib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/scib.metrics.pc_regression.html ; https://rdrr.io/github/theislab/kBET/man/pcRegression.html

label: PITFALL PC1 equals sequencing depth on raw counts
text: PITFALL: PCA on raw or poorly normalised scRNA-seq counts makes PC1 track sequencing depth / number of detected genes rather than the design factors, which changes every factor's R-squared on PC1. Here X holds raw counts. CHECK: confirm X is raw (integer values), apply library-size normalisation + log1p before PCA, then correlate PC1 with log total counts and gene_count; note that depth also differs biologically between cell types, so a correlation is not proof of artefact. IF FOUND (PC1 is mostly depth after normalisation): do not regress depth out blindly; instead re-run with an alternative transform (e.g. Pearson residuals or scaled HVGs) and report whether the factor ranking is unchanged. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-017-02554-5 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10172138/ ; https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-019-1861-6 ; https://doi.org/10.1101/576827

label: PITFALL uncentred sparse SVD gives wrong PC1
text: PITFALL: Running an uncentred SVD (sklearn TruncatedSVD, or scanpy pca with zero_center=False) on a sparse matrix returns a first component that mainly represents the vector of gene means, not the leading axis of variation, so 'PC1' is the wrong component. CHECK: verify the PCA call centres the genes (scanpy sc.pp.pca / sc.tl.pca default zero_center=True uses implicit centring on sparse input; sklearn PCA centres, TruncatedSVD does not); confirm PC1 scores have mean ~0. IF FOUND: redo with a centred PCA (arpack solver, fixed random_state) before computing any R-squared. SOURCE: https://github.com/theislab/scanpy/issues/393 ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.pca.html

label: snRNA marker detection is gene-specific; panel mean deflated
text: PITFALL: In single-nucleus RNA-seq, marker genes validated in whole cells are not equally detectable in nuclei: some transcripts are depleted in nuclei relative to whole cells (rapidly exported, mostly cytoplasmic mature mRNA), so a canonical marker can read near zero in the very cell type it marks; a panel average over 4-5 genes is then dragged down by the undetected genes even if one panel gene is strongly and specifically expressed in one cluster. CHECK: build a cluster x gene table for all 32 panel genes (mean log-normalized expression AND fraction of nuclei with count>0); flag genes that are near zero in every cluster; for each lineage look for a cluster where a single panel gene is high and specific (high fold-change vs all other clusters) while the panel mean still loses the argmax. IF FOUND: report the count the specified panel-mean argmax gives, but do not interpret a zero/low count as absence of the cell type; interpret from per-gene evidence (per-gene z-score across clusters, max-marker or rank-based scoring, snRNA-validated markers) and say which genes were non-informative in nuclei. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8805720/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-21595-1 ; https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/server/api/core/bitstreams/4b8b80c0-4acf-4b6e-b770-fe0a4b1a58c2/content

label: PITFALL R2 inflation for many-level factors
text: PITFALL: Unadjusted R-squared / eta-squared is biased upward by the number of levels: under no effect its expected value is (k-1)/(n-1), so a 91-level factor (cytokine) gains spurious variance relative to 12-level donor or 2-level treatment. At the single-cell level (n=100,000) this is ~0.09% and harmless, but on pseudobulk samples (n=1092) it is 90/1091 = ~8% for cytokine versus ~1% for donor, enough to flip a close ranking. CHECK: alongside raw R-squared compute adjusted R-squared (or omega-squared) and a label-permutation null R-squared for each factor at whatever unit of analysis is used. IF FOUND that raw and adjusted rankings differ: trust the adjusted/permutation-corrected ranking and say so; if using variancePartition-style joint models, model all categorical factors as random effects, never many-level fixed effects. SOURCE: https://janhove.github.io/posts/2016-04-22-r-squared/index.html ; https://jasonfinley.com/pubs/KroesFinley2023_OmegaSquared.pdf ; https://rdrr.io/bioc/variancePartition/f/vignettes/FAQ.Rmd

label: Raw panel means are not comparable across panels
text: PITFALL: Raw mean log-normalized expression is not comparable across different marker panels: a panel made of abundant genes scores high everywhere, a raw gene-set mean tracks sequencing depth and baseline expression level of its genes, and there is no background control, so an argmax across panels is biased toward panels with highly expressed or ubiquitously detected genes. CHECK: recompute cluster assignment three ways - (a) raw panel mean as specified, (b) per-gene z-score across clusters then panel mean, (c) scanpy.tl.score_genes (control-gene-subtracted) averaged per cluster - and list the clusters whose label flips; also print the winning margin (top score minus runner-up) per cluster. IF FOUND: keep the specified method for the number that is asked for, but treat lineages that only appear under (b)/(c) as evidence that the zero/low count is a scoring artifact rather than biology, and say so in the interpretation. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.tl.score_genes.html ; https://piaso.org/tutorials/gene-set-scoring/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12951948/

label: PITFALL treatment nested in cytokine
text: PITFALL: Treatment (PBS vs cytokine) is very likely a coarsening of the cytokine column (sample count 1092 = 12 donors x 91 cytokine levels suggests PBS is itself one of the 91 levels), and sample = donor x cytokine. A nested, coarser factor can never have a larger marginal R-squared than the finer factor it is nested in, and putting both in one model is rank-deficient (variancePartition aborts on collinearity > 0.99). CHECK: crosstab cytokine x treatment to see whether each cytokine level maps to exactly one treatment level. IF FOUND: compute each factor's R-squared in its own one-factor model; do not fit treatment and cytokine jointly or interpret a partial R-squared for treatment given cytokine (it is zero by construction); expect treatment <= cytokine as a mathematical necessity, not a biological finding. SOURCE: https://rdrr.io/bioc/variancePartition/f/vignettes/FAQ.Rmd ; https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/variancePartition/inst/doc/variancePartition.html

label: Ambient RNA floor favours abundant-lineage panels
text: PITFALL: Ambient RNA is pervasive in single-nucleus data and is dominated by the most abundant lineages of the tissue (in neural tissue: neuronal and glial transcripts), so markers of abundant lineages appear at a non-zero floor in every cluster and can outscore a rare lineage own panel; this has caused published mis-annotations of glia in brain snRNA-seq. CHECK: look at neuron/SGC/myelin panel genes in clusters that are clearly another lineage (e.g. the cluster with highest Pecam1/Cldn5 or C1qa/Csf1r); if those clusters still show substantial Snap25/Apoe/Mbp/Mpz-type signal, an ambient floor is present; compare each panel score to its minimum across clusters. IF FOUND: the filtered h5ad has no empty droplets so CellBender/SoupX cannot be run properly; instead subtract the per-gene across-cluster floor or z-score per gene before comparing panels, and state that the raw argmax is contaminated by ambient signal. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/neuron/fulltext/S0896-6273(22)00815-7 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41593-022-01232-0 ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-023-02978-x

label: PITFALL non-orthogonal factors and order-dependent SS
text: PITFALL: In an unbalanced design the factors are not orthogonal (cell-type composition differs between donors and possibly between cytokines), so variance shared between factors is counted in each marginal R-squared, and sequential (Type I) sums of squares change with the order terms are entered; the decomposition is not unique. CHECK: crosstab donor x cell_type and cytokine x cell_type (chi-square / Cramer's V); compare the marginal one-factor R-squared ranking with drop-one (partial) R-squared from the additive model PC1 ~ cell_type + donor + cytokine, and with a random-effects variance-component fit (PVCA / variancePartition style). IF FOUND that rankings disagree: report the marginal per-factor R-squared as the primary answer (it is what PC-regression tools compute), never a Type I table in arbitrary order, and flag the disagreement. SOURCE: https://sites.stat.columbia.edu/gelman/research/unpublished/econanova.pdf ; https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/j.1365-2656.2009.01634.x ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4911391/ ; https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/pvca/inst/doc/pvca.pdf

label: Gene-length / pre-mRNA bias in nuclei
text: PITFALL: snRNA-seq quantified with intronic reads has a gene-length bias: pre-mRNA is captured by internal priming roughly in proportion to gene length, so long genes are over-counted and short or intron-poor genes are under-detected in nuclei compared with whole cells; marker lists found in nuclei are systematically longer genes than marker lists found in cells. A panel that mixes long and short genes therefore has unequal per-gene sensitivity for a purely technical reason. CHECK: for each panel gene record dataset-wide detection rate (fraction of nuclei with count>0) and total counts, and compare within a panel; a panel where one gene is detected well and the others barely at all is suspect. IF FOUND: treat low values of the poorly detected genes as missing information, not as evidence against the lineage; do not let them vote equally in an average. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10984380/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11247185/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10132733/

label: PITFALL cell-level vs pseudobulk unit of analysis
text: PITFALL: The unit of analysis changes the answer. Pseudobulking per sample (donor x cytokine) removes cell type as a testable factor and converts cell-type composition differences into apparent donor/cytokine variance; pseudobulking per sample x cell type here averages only ~5 cells per group (100,000 cells / (1092 samples x 18 types)), with many empty or 1-cell groups, so those profiles are dominated by sampling noise. Because cell type is one of the factors to be ranked, the PCA units must vary in cell type. CHECK: tabulate cells per sample and per sample x cell_type before choosing; state the unit explicitly. IF FOUND that groups are this thin: use cell-level PCA as the primary analysis (all four factors are defined per cell), and treat any pseudobulk (e.g. donor x cell_type or cytokine x cell_type with a minimum-cells filter) only as a sensitivity check. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/conditions/differential%5Fgene%5Fexpression.html ; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9

label: Mural vs fibroblast marker overlap must be tested
text: PITFALL: Mural cells (pericytes, vascular smooth muscle) and fibroblasts share mesenchymal markers: Pdgfrb is high in both, and Acta2 and Cspg4 are also not mural-specific, so mural cells can be absorbed into a fibroblast-labelled cluster - but this explanation must be tested, not assumed, because it competes with the explanation that the panel average itself fails. CHECK: find the cluster where each mural panel gene peaks and record which lineage won that cluster and by what margin. If the mural-marker-high nuclei sit inside a cluster that also has high Col1a1/Col1a2/Pdgfra/Dcn, that supports fibroblast absorption; if the mural-marker-high cluster is separate from the collagen-high cluster and was won by a different panel, or lost only because the other mural genes are near zero, fibroblast overlap is not the cause. Also test whether the same cluster is low for fibroblast genes. IF FOUND: sub-cluster the fibroblast cluster or score with mural-vs-fibroblast discriminating genes before concluding. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-17740-1 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10041340/ ; https://doi.org/10.1007/s11427-020-1823-2

label: PITFALL imbalanced binary factor caps R2
text: PITFALL: R-squared of a binary factor depends on the group split, not only on effect size: with a very unbalanced split (PBS control is expected to be only ~1/91 of samples) the attainable variance explained is strongly attenuated, so a low R-squared for treatment does not mean no treatment effect, and it is not comparable as an effect size to balanced factors. CHECK: value_counts of treatment (and of every factor) to see the balance. IF FOUND: still report the observed R-squared for the ranking (the question asks about variance explained in this dataset), but do not subsample PBS/cytokine to 50:50 or reweight, because that changes the PCA and the quantity being ranked; mention the base-rate cap in the interpretation. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-015-0627-7 ; https://doi.org/10.1080/00220973.1986.10806427 ; https://ruscio.pages.tcnj.edu/files/2016/08/Ruscio-2008-PM-Probability-Based-ES.pdf

label: Test rarity/resolution explanations directly
text: PITFALL: A zero or low count for a rare lineage is often blamed on rarity or on clustering resolution without checking; modularity-based Leiden can merge small populations at low resolution, but raising resolution also splits noise, and a population can equally be present as its own cluster and simply be mislabelled. CHECK: independently of the panel argmax, count nuclei that express the best-detected lineage-specific marker(s), and see whether they are concentrated in one Leiden cluster at resolution 0.8 (cross-tabulate marker-positive nuclei by cluster; report cluster size and fraction positive). Then rerun Leiden at higher resolution (e.g. 1.5, 2.0) and repeat the argmax. IF FOUND: if a coherent marker-enriched cluster already exists at 0.8, neither rarity nor resolution explains the result and the annotation rule is at fault; if the assignment only changes at higher resolution, resolution is the cause; if marker-positive nuclei are few and scattered, rarity is plausible. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/cellular_structure/clustering.html ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/latest/api/generated/scanpy.tl.leiden.html

label: PITFALL PC1 depends on HVG and scaling choices
text: PITFALL: PC1 is not unique to the data; it depends on preprocessing choices on which the field has no consensus: highly-variable-gene selection (and its batch_key), per-gene scaling to unit variance (equal weight for all genes) versus unscaled log-counts (PC1 driven by highly expressed, highly variable genes), and clipping (max_value). A ranking that holds under only one pipeline is fragile. CHECK: compute the four per-factor R-squared values on PC1 under at least two or three reasonable pipelines (e.g. normalize_total + log1p + 2000 HVGs + scale + PCA; the same without scaling; all genes) and check that PC1 is not dominated by one rare cell type or a few outlier cells. IF FOUND that the ranking changes between pipelines: report the standard default pipeline (normalize_total, log1p, HVG, scale, centred PCA) as primary, and state which pairs of factors are close enough to swap. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2164 ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/tutorials/basics/clustering.html ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.scale.html

label: Leiden / HVG choices change cluster-summed counts
text: PITFALL: Leiden output is not unique: cluster number and membership change with random seed, implementation (leidenalg vs igraph flavor, n_iterations, directed), scanpy version, n_neighbors/n_pcs, HVG flavor (dispersion flavors expect log data, seurat_v3 expects raw counts), and whether data are scaled before PCA; published tests show a large share of cells change cluster across seeds. A per-lineage nucleus count that is a sum over whole clusters can jump when one cluster flips label. CHECK: run the exact specified workflow with scanpy defaults (random_state 0), then repeat with 3-5 seeds and with the other Leiden flavor / HVG flavor / with and without sc.pp.scale, and tabulate the count of interest in each run. IF FOUND: report the default-pipeline number, state how stable it is, and note the two teams may differ for this reason alone; a count that is the same (for instance zero) in every variant is robust. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11014608/ ; https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.06.16.732539v1.full.pdf ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes.html ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/1531

label: Gene-symbol mapping and matrix used for scoring
text: PITFALL: Panel scores can be computed on the wrong matrix or the wrong genes. In /workspace/data/illumina_pipseeker.h5ad (19,259 nuclei x 32,227 genes, X = raw integer counts, samples 3M, 21M1, 21M2) var_names are Ensembl IDs and symbols live in var[gene_symbol], which has only 32,200 unique values for 32,227 rows (duplicated symbols); subsetting to the 3,000 HVGs (subset=True) drops most panel genes, and sc.pp.scale replaces log-normalized values with z-scores. A silently missing gene changes the panel denominator. CHECK: confirm each of the 32 panel genes maps to exactly one var row (case-sensitive mouse symbols), keep the full log-normalized matrix in a layer or adata.raw before HVG subsetting/scaling, and compute panel means from that layer over all found genes. IF FOUND: resolve duplicates explicitly (do not let var_names_make_unique rename a panel gene unnoticed), report any gene that is absent, and never score from the scaled or HVG-only matrix. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/tutorials/basics/clustering.html (file header inspected directly)

label: Minimal QC: doublet / low-quality / sample-driven clusters
text: PITFALL: The provided data were filtered only by n_genes_by_counts > 1000 (no doublet, mitochondrial or UMI-outlier filtering, no integration across the three samples of two ages), so some Leiden clusters may be heterotypic doublets, ambient-dominated/damaged nuclei or sample-driven; such clusters show mixed lineage markers and are labelled arbitrarily by a panel argmax, and a real small population can be hidden in a doublet-like cluster. CHECK: per cluster report median total counts and genes, sample composition (3M vs 21M1 vs 21M2), and co-expression of mutually exclusive lineage markers; optionally run Scrublet per sample (not on pooled samples). IF FOUND: flag those clusters and exclude them from the biological interpretation, but do not silently drop them from the requested count - the task asks for the exploratory workflow on the first-pass filtered object. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12574873/

label: Do not assume isolation depletion without checking marker-positive nuclei
text: PITFALL: Cell-type composition in nuclei preparations differs from whole-cell preparations (for example a mouse lung comparison recovered very different epithelial vs immune proportions by snRNA-seq and scRNA-seq), which makes it tempting to explain a missing lineage as selective loss during nuclear isolation; that claim cannot be established from an expression matrix alone and is contradicted if nuclei carrying the lineage signature are in fact present. CHECK: before invoking isolation loss, count nuclei positive for the best-detected lineage-specific marker and check whether they form a coherent cluster with supporting co-markers. IF FOUND: if such nuclei exist in appreciable number, reject the depletion explanation and look at the annotation rule; only if marker-positive nuclei are essentially absent is depletion (or true rarity) tenable. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7790136/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9846005/

label: PITFALL endothelial-mural cross-contamination
text: PITFALL: Endothelial cells and mural cells (pericytes/SMC) are physically attached, so mural clusters in single-cell/nucleus data routinely carry endothelial transcripts (attached fragments, EC-mural doublets), and vice versa; a gene specific to one vascular type then shows up in the other and the endothelial-vs-mural ranking of a gene can be decided by contamination rather than biology. CHECK: in the nuclei labelled Mural, compute the fraction with any Pecam1/Flt1 counts (and in Endothelial the fraction with Rgs5/Notch3); recompute mean log1p(CP10K) Edn1 per type after dropping nuclei that co-express both marker sets, and look at whether Edn1-positive mural nuclei are the Pecam1/Flt1-positive ones. IF FOUND: sub-cluster the vascular clusters and relabel/remove the mixed sub-cluster before taking the per-type mean; report the ranking with and without the co-expressing nuclei and trust the one that is stable. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature25739 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11452347/

label: PITFALL mixed clusters at one resolution
text: PITFALL: At a single moderate resolution (0.6) one Leiden/Louvain cluster can contain two major cell types (typical merges: endothelial+mural, SGC+Schwann, fibroblast+mural, immune types together), and one-label-per-cluster by top marker score then silently assigns the minority type's nuclei to the majority label, shifting both per-type means. CHECK: for every cluster print, per marker gene, the fraction of nuclei with count>0 and mean log1p(CP10K) for ALL nine marker sets (not only the winner); flag clusters where a second marker set is detected in >~15-20% of nuclei or where per-nucleus marker scores are bimodal inside the cluster. IF FOUND: sub-cluster the flagged cluster (higher resolution on that subset only) and label the sub-clusters separately; also do not force all nine labels to exist - T_cell/B_cell may have no cluster of their own in ganglion nuclei data. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.31219/osf.io/ndafw ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11452347/

label: PITFALL use raw-derived lognorm not integrated values
text: PITFALL: After integration the per-cell-type expression is computed from the wrong matrix - the integrated/batch-corrected values, z-scored scale.data, or a matrix already subset to highly variable genes (Edn1 may not be an HVG, and CP10K computed after gene subsetting uses the wrong denominator). Integrated values are shifted by anchor-weighted corrections and are for clustering/visualisation only. CHECK: confirm the Edn1 vector used in Step 5 comes from log1p(counts / total_counts_over_all_32227_genes * 1e4) of the raw matrix; it must be >=0, exactly 0 where the raw Edn1 count is 0, and expm1 of each nucleus's row must sum to 1e4. IF FOUND: keep a full-gene raw-count copy before HVG selection/scaling/integration, compute the log1p(CP10K) Edn1 vector from it once, and use integration output only to get cluster labels. SOURCE: https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/discussions/4000 ; https://sib-swiss.github.io/single-cell-training-archived/latest/day2/integration/

label: PITFALL log-space vs linear-space cluster mean
text: PITFALL: 'Average expression per cluster' is not one number: Seurat AverageExpression on the data layer exponentiates first (mean of expm1, i.e. linear space), whereas the task asks for the plain mean of log1p(CP10K) values. For a sparse gene the two can rank cell types differently (linear-space mean is dominated by a few high nuclei; log-space mean tracks the fraction of expressing nuclei). CHECK: for Edn1 per major type compute (a) mean(log1p CP10K) over all nuclei including zeros, (b) log1p(mean(expm1)), (c) fraction of nuclei with count>0, (d) mean among expressing nuclei; see whether the top type is the same in all. IF FOUND (rankings disagree): answer with (a) as the task specifies, never (d) and never AverageExpression defaults, and say in the notes that the ranking is metric-dependent. SOURCE: https://satijalab.org/seurat/reference/averageexpression ; https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/4181

label: PITFALL log1p depth bias across cell types
text: PITFALL: The mean of log1p(CP10K) is systematically biased by sequencing depth: cell types with very different UMI totals per nucleus (in ganglia, neurons have far more UMIs than glia/vascular/immune nuclei) get different mean log-values for the same true relative expression, so small between-type differences in a low-count gene can be depth artefacts. CHECK: tabulate median total_counts per major type; compute a depth-robust pseudobulk for Edn1 per type (sum of Edn1 counts / sum of total counts * 1e4) and the fraction of expressing nuclei, and compare the ranking with the mean-log1p ranking. IF FOUND (top type changes or the margin is small): still report the task-specified mean log1p(CP10K), but only call the answer secure if pseudobulk and detection fraction agree; flag it otherwise. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1101/404962 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10172138/

label: PITFALL ambient RNA baseline in snRNA-seq
text: PITFALL: Ambient RNA in snRNA-seq spreads transcripts of abundant/fragile cell types into every nucleus, so non-source types show a low uniform 'soup' level of a gene and rare cell types look like they express genes of abundant ones; this has caused wrong annotations and can also make a marker-based label wrong (e.g. neuronal markers in glia). CHECK: measure contamination by the fraction of non-neuronal nuclei with neuronal marker counts (Prph, Isl1, or other strong neuron genes) and SGC markers in non-SGC nuclei; for Edn1 compare the top type's mean and detection fraction against the near-constant baseline across the other types. Only a filtered matrix (no empty droplets) is provided, so SoupX/CellBender cannot be run properly; DecontX-style correction is the only option. IF FOUND: label clusters by relative enrichment (cluster vs rest) rather than presence/absence of a marker, and treat a top type that exceeds the baseline by only a small margin as unreliable. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9789184/ ; https://www.10xgenomics.com/analysis-guides/introduction-to-ambient-rna-correction

label: PITFALL doublet clusters distort labels
text: PITFALL: Heterotypic doublets (two nuclei of different types in one droplet) form their own clusters that co-express two marker sets; the n_genes>1000 filter enriches for them because doublets have more genes. Such a cluster gets forced into one major label and contaminates that type's mean. CHECK: per cluster compare median n_genes/total_counts with other clusters and look for strong co-expression of two lineages' markers (neuron+SGC, endothelial+mural, Schwann+fibroblast); optionally run Scrublet/scDblFinder per sample and see whether flagged nuclei concentrate in one cluster. IF FOUND: label that cluster doublet/unassigned and exclude it from the per-type means (the task does not ask for doublet removal, so report the answer both with and without it and state if it changes). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7897250/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6625319/

label: PITFALL uneven marker sets and nuclear detection bias

reason: A team using a package default for 'average expression' would compute a different statistic from the one the task specifies and could select a different cell type.
text: The task's statistic is the plain arithmetic mean of log1p(CP10K) Edn1 over ALL nuclei of a major type, zeros included. Do not use Seurat AverageExpression defaults (it exponentiates first, i.e. averages in linear space) and do not use the mean among expressing nuclei only. For a sparsely detected gene these metrics can rank cell types differently: the linear-space mean is dominated by a few high nuclei, the log-space mean tracks the fraction of expressing nuclei. Check: per major type compute (a) mean log1p(CP10K) over all nuclei, (b) log1p(mean(expm1)), (c) fraction of nuclei with Edn1 count > 0, (d) mean among expressing nuclei. reason: The integration step is the least portable part of the recipe; the team needs to know how to label sample-specific clusters and to test that the result does not hinge on the integration method.
text: RPCA integration caveats. (1) Scanpy has no native RPCA anchor integration, so a Python pipeline has to substitute or re-implement it and will get clusters that differ from a Seurat run; say which method you actually used. (2) Seurat's RPCA is deliberately conservative (default k.anchor=5), so the same cell type can stay split into sample-specific clusters; IntegrateData also fails if a batch has fewer cells than k.weight=100. Check: cross-tabulate cluster x sample. A cluster that is >90% from one sample and carries the same markers as another cluster is under-correction, not a new cell type: give it the same major label by markers (the major-type means are then unaffected) or raise k.anchor (e.g. 20). Also repeat the labelling with a second integration (e.g. Harmony, or none) and confirm the per-type Edn1 ranking does not change. The Edn1 values come from raw counts; only the labels depend on integration, so the integration choice should not be what decides the answer.

reason: The per-type Edn1 means depend entirely on the cluster labels; a naive scoring rule over this uneven marker list in ambient-contaminated nuclei can mislabel clusters.
text: Label clusters by relative enrichment, not by marker presence or by argmax of a raw marker-set mean. Reasons: (1) ambient RNA in snRNA-seq spreads transcripts of abundant types (e.g. neuronal Prph/Isl1, SGC markers) at a low uniform level into every nucleus, so presence/absence gives wrong labels; (2) the marker sets are uneven: Schwann has four markers covering two subtypes (Mag, Ncmap = myelinating; Scn7a, L1cam = non-myelinating), so a plain set average penalises every Schwann cluster against the two-marker types; (3) some markers are poorly captured in nuclei (documented for macrophage/microglial genes), and Rgs5 and Pecam1 are not exclusive to one type. Do this: for each cluster and each marker compute fold-enrichment and detection fraction versus all other nuclei; accept a label only when at least one marker of that set is clearly enriched and the other sets are not; for ambiguous clusters use max-over-markers or per-gene z-scores across clusters, and settle ties with the cluster's own top differentially expressed genes. The same ambient baseline applies to Edn1: compare the top type's mean and detection fraction with the near-constant low level seen in the other types, and treat a lead of only a small margin over that baseline as unreliable. Only a filtered matrix is provided, so SoupX/CellBender cannot be run properly.

reason: A merged cluster changes the membership of two major types at once, which directly changes the per-type Edn1 means being compared.
text: At resolution 0.6 a single cluster can contain two major cell types (typical merges: endothelial+mural, SGC+Schwann, fibroblast+mural, several immune types together). One label per cluster then silently moves the minority type's nuclei into the majority label and shifts both types' means. Check: for every cluster print, for ALL nine marker sets (not only the winning one), the fraction of nuclei with count > 0 and the mean log1p(CP10K) of each marker; flag clusters where a second marker set is detected in more than about 15-20% of nuclei or where per-nucleus marker scores are bimodal within the cluster. If found: sub-cluster only that cluster at higher resolution and label the sub-clusters separately. Do not force all nine labels to exist; T_cell and B_cell may have no cluster of their own in ganglion nuclei data.

reason: Mixed nuclei forced into one major label contaminate that type's Edn1 mean; the team needs a concrete test for whether such nuclei are driving the ranking.
text: Cross-lineage contamination of a labelled type. (1) Heterotypic doublets form their own clusters that co-express two marker sets, and the n_genes > 1000 filter enriches for them because doublets have more genes. Check per cluster: median n_genes and total counts against the other clusters, and strong co-expression of two lineages' markers (neuron+SGC, endothelial+mural, Schwann+fibroblast); optionally run Scrublet/scDblFinder per sample and see whether flagged nuclei concentrate in one cluster. (2) Endothelial and mural cells are physically attached, so each of these two types routinely carries the other's transcripts, and the relative ranking of a gene between the two can be set by contamination in either direction. Check: fraction of Mural-labelled nuclei with any Pecam1/Flt1 counts and of Endothelial-labelled nuclei with any Rgs5/Notch3 counts, and whether the Edn1-positive nuclei in either type are the ones co-expressing the other type's markers. If found: sub-cluster the vascular clusters and label mixed sub-clusters separately. The task does not ask for doublet removal and defines the mean over all nuclei of each labelled type, so report the per-type Edn1 ranking both with and without the co-expressing/doublet nuclei and state whether it changes.

QUESTION: In random-effects variance partitioning of a single response (as implemented in the variancePartition and PVCA approaches), how is the fraction of variance attributed to each crossed categorical factor defined, and when two factors are associated in an unbalanced design (for example group composition differing between levels of another factor), to which factor is the shared variance assigned compared with a one-factor-at-a-time R-squared? ANSWER: DEFINITION (sourced, high confidence). One linear mixed model is fitted to the response with every categorical factor as a random intercept, e.g. PC1 ~ (1|cell_type) + (1|donor) + (1|cytokine), using lme4::lmer. The fraction for factor k is its estimated variance component divided by the sum of all variance components plus the residual variance: sigma2_k / (sum_j sigma2_j + sigma2_residual). The fractions, residual included, sum to 1 and are always non-negative; each equals an intra-class correlation (the correlation of two observations sharing that factor level). The Gaussian prior shrinks per-level effects toward zero, which is why many-level factors are not over-credited as they are by fixed-effects least squares. PVCA uses the same variance-component fit (factors as random effects) on principal components and combines them with eigenvalue weights; on a single PC it reduces to the same per-factor fraction. SHARED VARIANCE (partly sourced, medium confidence). The vignette says each fraction is reported 'while simultaneously correcting for all other' variables, that 'like all multiple regression methods, variancePartition will divide the contribution over multiple variables that are strongly correlated', and that adding a correlated variable lowers the other's fraction (sex versus individual example). So the difference from one-factor-at-a-time R-squared is: marginal R-squared counts variance shared between associated factors in full in every one of them (the marginal values can sum above 1), while the joint variance-component fit counts it once. A factor whose marginal R-squared arises only because the composition of another factor differs across its levels (e.g. donors or cytokines differing in cell-type mix) keeps only what is left after the other factor is fitted, so its fraction drops below its marginal R-squared and the composition-driven share goes to the factor that actually carries the level effects (here cell type). That last sentence is my inference from the 'correcting for all others' statement; no page I read gives an explicit allocation formula for unbalanced crossed factors, so the web does not fully settle the exact split. NESTED FACTORS (sourced). A coarser factor nested in a finer one (sex within individual in the vignette; here treatment within cytokine) removes its share from the finer factor and the two fractions add up to the total between-level variation. The mixed model can fit such nested terms where a fixed-effects ANOVA is singular. Consequently, in a variance-component fit treatment is not mathematically bounded above by cytokine, unlike marginal R-squared. This refines the earlier department note that a joint treatment + cytokine model is unusable: that holds for fixed effects, not for random effects. NOT SOURCED (my statistical reasoning, low confidence): a variance component describes the spread of level effects and is not weighted by level sizes the way SS_between/SS_total is, so a very unbalanced 2-level factor can get a larger fraction than its marginal R-squared, but a component estimated from 2 levels is poorly determined. HOW SURE: high for the definition; medium for how shared variance is allocated (the sources say it is divided and each factor is adjusted for the others, but give no explicit rule for unbalanced crossed factors). SOURCES: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/variancePartition/inst/doc/variancePartition.html, https://bmcbioinformatics.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12859-016-1323-z, https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/pvca/inst/doc/pvca.pdf.

QUESTION: In split-pool combinatorial-barcoding single-cell RNA-seq, what do the round-1 barcode well and the sublibrary each represent experimentally, which of them is the recommended technical batch covariate, and are sublibrary effects on leading principal components commonly reported? ANSWER: ROUND-1 WELL (sourced, high confidence). Fixed cells of each sample are loaded into one or more wells of the first barcoding plate, where in-cell reverse transcription adds a well-specific barcode. Vendor material calls these 'sample-specific barcodes', and samples are demultiplexed by their round-1 wells. Round-1 well is therefore a label of sample identity (here donor x cytokine), nested in sample, not an independent technical batch; its effect cannot be separated from donor or condition unless one sample was spread over several wells. Rounds 2 and 3 are random re-splits of the pooled cells and carry no sample information. SUBLIBRARY (sourced, high confidence). After round 3 all cells are pooled, counted and split into aliquots called sublibraries (2, 8 or 16 depending on kit size). Each sublibrary is lysed, template-switched, cDNA-amplified (cycle number chosen per sublibrary), fragmented and indexed by PCR separately; the sublibrary index is the fourth barcode. Sublibraries can hold different numbers of cells and be sequenced separately and to different depths. Each sublibrary contains cells from every sample in roughly even proportion. WHICH IS THE BATCH COVARIATE (medium confidence, partly inference). Sublibrary is the true technical processing unit (separate lysis, amplification, library prep, possibly sequencing depth). No page I read explicitly recommends it as a batch covariate; that follows from the protocol. Because every sublibrary draws from all samples, sublibrary is crossed with donor and cytokine rather than confounded with them, so a sublibrary effect cannot by itself create a donor or condition association on a principal component. Round-1 well is the opposite: fully confounded with sample, so using it as a 'batch' factor would absorb donor and cytokine signal. ARE SUBLIBRARY EFFECTS ON LEADING PCs COMMONLY REPORTED (not settled, low confidence). Two searches found no report of sublibrary effects driving leading principal components, and none of the pages read describe one. Absence in ten calls is weak evidence, so I cannot say they are rare. The documented way sublibraries differ is cell number and sequencing depth, so the practical check is sublibrary against total counts / genes detected, then sublibrary R-squared on PC1. HOW SURE: high for what round-1 well and sublibrary represent; medium for sublibrary being the right technical covariate (implied by protocol, not stated as a recommendation); low for how commonly sublibrary effects on leading PCs are reported (web did not settle it). text: FINDING: Seurat RPCA anchor integration does NOT use a single reference by default. FindIntegrationAnchors has reference=NULL: 'all pairwise anchors are found (no reference/s)'; IntegrateData then does iterative pairwise integration in an order set by a guide tree computed automatically (sample.tree=NULL): distance between two datasets = cells in the smaller dataset / number of anchors between them, and that distance matrix is hierarchically clustered. Only when reference is given are anchors found between each query and the reference(s), the references integrated pairwise, and each query mapped onto the integrated reference - so a fixed largest-batch reference is a documented option, not the default (with 3 batches the default finds 3 anchor sets and merges the two most anchor-rich batches first). text: FINDING: Yes, the ceiling is real and is a general theorem (Samuelson's inequality): among n values none can lie more than (n-1)/sqrt(n) sample standard deviations (1/(n-1) SD; sqrt(n-1) with the 1/n SD) from their mean, and equality holds exactly when the other n-1 values are all equal - i.e. a marker confined to one cluster. So after z-scoring cluster means across N clusters, every gene (or marker-set mean) that is flat outside one cluster gets the identical score (N-1)/sqrt(N) whatever its expression level (2.67 for N=9, 3.61 for N=15), and two marker sets that are both specific to the same cluster tie at the ceiling: the across-cluster z-score cannot rank them. Seurat's developers acknowledge the same effect for DotPlot: it averages the data slot per group, z-scores the group averages (scale=TRUE default, so the number of points scaled equals the number of groups) and clips to col.min/col.max = -2.5/2.5; with two groups the values are always +-0.707, a developer agreed this 'can definitely lead to misleading results, and becomes more extreme as the number of groups gets lower' and added a warning for fewer than 5 groups. I found no single-cell documentation that names the (N-1)/sqrt(N) saturation as a limitation of marker-set ranking; that part is the theorem applied. Documented conventions, none of which is a mandated one-label rule: Seurat DotPlot (dot size = percent of cells expressing, colour = scaled average expression); scanpy dotplot (colour = mean expression in group, unscaled by default with standard_scale=None; size = fraction of cells expressing); Seurat AddModuleScore (per-cell mean of the set minus mean of control genes drawn from the same average-expression bin, nbin=24, ctrl=100, seed=1); scanpy score_genes (same idea after Tirosh 2016, ctrl_size=50, n_bins=25, gene_pool = all genes). To break a ceiling tie use quantities that are not bounded by N: unscaled mean log expression and detection fraction per marker in that cluster, fold-change versus the rest, or per-nucleus module scores averaged per cluster. Confidence: high for the mathematics and tool definitions, medium that it is a recognised limitation in single-cell practice. QUESTION: What are the documented conventions for assigning one cell-type label per cluster from short marker lists, and is it a known limitation that z-scoring cluster means across clusters saturates near (N-1)/sqrt(N) for a marker restricted to one cluster so it cannot rank two marker sets specific to the same cluster? question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: What are the documented conventions for assigning one cell-type label per cluster from short marker lists (average of scaled expression per cluster, module scores with expression-matched control genes such as AddModuleScore or scanpy score_genes, detection-fraction dot plots), and is it a known limitation that z-scoring cluster means across clusters saturates near (N-1)/sqrt(N) for a marker restricted to one cluster, so that it cannot rank two marker sets that are both specific to the same cluster? ANSWER: The ceiling is real and is a general theorem (Samuelson's inequality): among n values, none lies more than (n-1)/sqrt(n) sample standard deviations from the mean (sqrt(n-1) with the 1/n standard deviation), with equality exactly when the other n-1 values are all equal, which is the case of a marker confined to one cluster. After z-scoring cluster means across N clusters, every gene or marker-set mean that is flat outside one cluster gets the same score (N-1)/sqrt(N), whatever its expression level (2.67 for N=9, 3.61 for N=15). Two marker sets that are both specific to the same cluster tie at that ceiling, so the across-cluster z-score cannot rank them. Seurat's developers acknowledge the same effect in DotPlot: it averages the data slot per group, z-scores the group averages (scale=TRUE by default, so the number of points scaled equals the number of groups) and clips to col.min/col.max = -2.5/2.5; with two groups the values are always +-0.707, and a developer agreed this 'can definitely lead to misleading results, and becomes more extreme as the number of groups gets lower' and added a warning for fewer than 5 groups. I found no single-cell documentation that names the (N-1)/sqrt(N) saturation as a limitation of marker-set ranking; that part is the theorem applied to this case. Conventions that are documented, none of them a mandated one-label-per-cluster rule: Seurat DotPlot (dot size = percentage of cells expressing, colour = scaled average expression); scanpy dotplot (colour = mean expression in the group, unscaled by default with standard_scale=None, size = fraction of cells expressing); Seurat AddModuleScore (per-cell mean of the set minus the mean of control genes drawn from the same average-expression bin; nbin=24, ctrl=100, seed=1); scanpy score_genes (same approach after Tirosh 2016; ctrl_size=50, n_bins=25, gene_pool = all genes). Labelling a cluster is treated as a judgement combining mean expression and detection fraction. To break a ceiling tie, use quantities not bounded by N: unscaled mean log expression and detection fraction per marker in that cluster, fold-change against the rest, or per-nucleus module scores averaged per cluster. Not read in full: the scanpy clustering tutorial's annotation section and the text of scanpy's standard_scale option (pages were cut short). HOW SURE: high for the mathematics and the tool definitions; medium that it is a recognised limitation in single-cell practice. SOURCES: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuelson%27s_inequality, https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/5742, https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/7571, https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/783, https://satijalab.org/seurat/reference/dotplot, https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/generated/scanpy.pl.dotplot.html, https://satijalab.org/seurat/reference/addmodulescore, https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/generated/scanpy.tl.score_genes.html, https://ouyanglab.com/singlecell/clust.html.

A 2025 IEEE TCBB paper on scRNA-seq kNN graphs states (abstract only; body not accessible) that the minimum resolution at which a roughly disconnected subgraph splits off is inversely proportional to its frequency in the graph, i.e. rarer populations need higher resolution.

Caveats: these results describe the optimum of Q; Leiden is a heuristic optimiser, and on a weighted kNN graph the outcome also depends on n_neighbors and edge weights, so no formula read here converts resolution 0.8 into a cell count for a given dataset. Implication for the clause being tested: a resolution-limit explanation applies only if the small population is merged into a larger cluster at 0.8; the resolution limit says nothing about whether a small cluster that already exists can be annotated, and the specific figure of ~100 nuclei has no source. HOW SURE: Part A: medium (negative result from a limited search; no source read states such a threshold). Part B: high for the quality function, merge condition and sqrt(N/gamma) scaling (read in the leidenalg reference and two papers); medium for how closely Leiden on a weighted, directed kNN graph follows these idealised bounds.. Mural wins the argmax only if the mural fraction exceeds 42% with all four genes and 35% without Acta2 (same 35% if Acta2 in pericytes is set to the mean of the other three); the actual fraction is 19%. At the actual mix the mural deficit is 0.70 (0.53 vs 1.23); removing the near-zero gene closes 0.11 of it (about 16%), mixing accounts for the other ~84%. Acta2 is not a nuclear-detection failure: the 30 nuclei with >=3 smooth-muscle contractile genes (Myh11, Tagln, Cnn1, Des, Actg2, Lmod1, Myocd) have Acta2 detected in 83% (mean 2.22); 17 of them sit in cluster 16 and 6 in fibroblast cluster 8; only 158 nuclei (0.8%) detect Acta2 at all, 41 in cluster 16 of which just 5 in the pericyte subcluster. So Acta2 is low in pericytes because capillary pericytes express little of it, while the few smooth-muscle nuclei carry it. Cluster 22 Rgs5 is carried by the neurons: 96% of its 211 nuclei are Rgs5-positive at the same level as pericytes (median 2.67), with Notch3 1.5%, Pdgfrb 3.9%, Kcnj8/Abcc9/Higd1b 0% versus 93/87/33/59/34% in pericytes, and Th 86%, Snap25 91%, P2ry1 89%; median UMIs 5174, below the neuron median 6324, so not doublets; Rgs5 is also detected in 37-64% of three other neuron clusters, so not ambient. Changes method: no. The deficit is mostly mixing with endothelial nuclei, not the near-zero gene.

text: REPLY (sc01-team-b) to the director's question on small clusters at resolution 0.8: only two clusters are below 150 nuclei. Cluster 26 (79 nuclei) is labelled Neuron by a margin of 0.02 (0.41 vs 0.39) but its top genes are Mki67, Top2a, Spta1, Kel, Ermap, Rhd, Hemgn, Hmbs, i.e. proliferating erythroid cells with no matching panel, so the label is wrong. Cluster 27 (39 nuclei, 38 from sample 3M) is labelled Neuron by 0.48 and its top genes (Gria2, Grin2b, Fgf14, Dlg2, Cacna1e) are neuronal (central-type), so the label is right at lineage level. Clusters 24 (154) and 25 (152) are Neuron by 0.91 and 0.77 with nociceptor genes (Osmr, Il31ra, Scn10a, Scn11a), correct. So the one bad small-cluster label comes from a cell type missing from the panels, not from size. The pericyte-like nuclei are not in a small cluster at 0.8 at all: they are 86 of the 459 nuclei of endothelial-labelled cluster 16 (469-516 across seeds). Changes method: no. It does change how I read option 5: its first clause (clusters under ~100 nuclei cannot be annotated) is not what happens here and has no library support; only its second clause (resolution 2.0 gives a mural-labelled cluster) is supported, and the true mechanism is merging of an ~86-nucleus population into a larger endothelial cluster at 0.8. I still rank option 5 first because options 1-4 each fail a direct check, but with lower confidence.

text: REPLY (sc01-team-b) to the director's question on rescoring with clusters held fixed at resolution 0.8 (28 clusters): no scoring rule gives the vascular cluster 16 the mural label. Mural vs Endothelial in cluster 16: panel mean 0.53 vs 1.23; z-score across cluster means 3.26 vs 4.98; z-score across nuclei 1.19 vs 2.88; max over markers 0.76 vs 2.44; mean detection fraction 0.22 vs 0.51; mural panel without Acta2 0.64 vs 1.23; every panel dropping its lowest gene 0.64 vs 1.49. The only rule that produces any mural label is the per-nucleus z-score, which labels cluster 22 (211 nuclei) Mural by 0.91 vs 0.84, and that is a false positive: cluster 22 is Th+ Rgs5+ C-LTMR neurons (top genes Rgs5, Rgs4, P2ry1, Th, Pou4f1, Fxyd2) with no pericyte co-markers. Max-over-markers leaves cluster 22 Neuron (2.50 vs 2.76). Changes method: no. A scoring change alone cannot recover mural cells at 0.8, which argues against the panel-averaging/nuclear-detection explanation (option 3) and for cluster granularity as the cause.

text: REPLY (sc01-team-a) to the director's fixed-cluster question (all eight lineages at res 0.8, and Rgs5 in cluster 22). Check run: per lineage, best cluster by z-scored panel, its top DE genes, raw label and per-gene detection. Neuron (c12), MyelSchwann (c2), Fibroblast (c19), Endothelial (c16) and SGC (c0/c10) have coherent clusters that the raw panel mean labels correctly. Macrophage: coherent cluster 6 exists (842 nuclei, top genes Ptprc, Dock2, Inpp5d, Ikzf1) but loses the argmax (0.41 vs MyelSchwann 0.45) because its panel genes are poorly detected in its own nuclei (C1qa 15, Aif1 5, Lyz2 36, Csf1r 36 percent) against an ambient Mpz/Mbp floor: a scoring failure with the clusters fixed. Mural: NO coherent mural cluster exists at 0.8; the best mural cluster is c16 whose top genes are endothelial (Flt1, Mecom, Emcn, Egfl7) and in which mural genes are detected in only 24-32 percent of nuclei because 81 percent of the cluster is not mural. Cluster 22 Rgs5 is neuronal, not pericyte contamination: 205 of 211 nuclei are Rgs5+, median counts 5396 match other neuron clusters (5459) rather than doublet-like inflation, pericyte co-markers Kcnj8, Abcc9, Vtn, Higd1b are detected in 0-1 percent (34-54 percent in true mural nuclei), Notch3 2 and Pdgfrb 4 percent with no increase in Rgs5-high nuclei, top genes Rgs5, Rgs4, Th, P2ry1, Pou4f1 (a Th+ sensory neuron subtype). So the mural zero is a different kind of failure from the macrophage one: macrophage = scoring rule defeats an existing cluster; mural = no separate cluster to score. Changes method: no. The fixed-cluster reading does not rescue the nuclear-detection explanation for mural, since changing only the scoring (drop Acta2, z-score, score_genes) still gives 0 mural nuclei.
